population: Every Bug-labelled ticket in the LinearViewer team (both repos) listed on 2026-09-30, 265 tickets, LIN-26 to LIN-3122.
method: Each ticket read from its title, labels, state, own merged PRs, description (first 3,500 chars) and the tickets it names, by five in-session subagents working one batch each against this rubric, fixed before reading. Not second-read; see the paper Limits.

rubric.escaped: reports a fault in behaviour already merged to main in either repo (code, prompt/template text, config, UI): wrong output, crash, hang, broken page, security or credential flaw, data loss, a shipped change that did not take effect, or a false close-out claim that hid a fault; found after merge and not filed from the shipping ticket's own review/close-out ledger. A fault in older code found while reviewing a different ticket is escaped.
rubric.escaped-test: the fault is only in tests, CI, fixtures or dev tooling.
rubric.routed: the fault was named by the review, plan-review or close-out of the very ticket that shipped it and filed from that ledger: the gate saw it and it shipped anyway.
rubric.not-defect: feature request, enhancement, research, docs-only, process or prompt-policy wish with no faulty behaviour, external/environment problem outside both repos, or duplicate.
rubric.introducedBy: the LIN id of the shipped change the text says introduced, exposed or left the fault unhandled, only if named. For escapes found by a later review (label kind:review-residue) it can name the reviewing ticket that deferred the fault rather than the one that wrote the code, so those rows are left out of the size, depth and merge-month analyses.
rubric.repo: where the faulty behaviour lives, from the ticket's own PRs first, then the text.
rubric.foundBy: human (the operator reports or observed it) / agent (a later agent session, another ticket's review, a periodical or monitor) / unclear.
